sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which of these is a percussion instrument?
When a dancer uses hand gestures to tell a story, it is called a:
What emotion are you showing if you are dancing with a wide smile and jumping high?
Which of these sounds is made by striking your hands together?
A musical piece that uses words to tell a story is often called a:
Which part of the body is primarily used for footwork in traditional dances?
If you want to make a soft, tinkling sound in music, what would you use?
What does 'tempo' mean in a song or dance?
options: B) How fast or slow it is
D) What color the stage is
questions.answer: B) How fast or slow it is

questions.question_text: Which physical action best expresses sadness in a dance performance?
options: B) Looking down and moving slowly
questions.answer: B) Looking down and moving slowly

questions.question_text: Which of these is a string instrument?
How can you use everyday objects from your home to make music? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: We can tap wooden spoons together, shake a plastic bottle filled with dry rice, or hit an empty plastic bucket with sticks to make fun, rhythmic beats.

questions.question_text: Describe how your face looks when expressing surprise during a dance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To show surprise in a dance, I would open my eyes very wide, lift my eyebrows up high, and open my mouth in a big round 'O' shape.

questions.question_text: Name two different ways you can move across a stage and how they feel. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I can skip across the stage, which feels light and happy. I can also stomp heavily, which feels strong, powerful, and sometimes a little angry.

questions.question_text: Why is having a steady drumbeat important in a group dance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A drumbeat is very important because it gives the dancers a steady rhythm to follow, helping everyone move together in perfect timing and stay synchronized.

questions.question_text: How do you show you are a strong, unmoving tree using only your body? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I stand very still with my legs firmly planted on the ground like deep roots. I stretch my arms up high and wide like strong branches reaching for the sun.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are writing a song about a rainy day. Describe the sounds you would include and what instruments you would use to make them. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: For my rainy day song, I would use a shaker filled with small beads to sound like gentle rain falling. I would lightly tap a xylophone for the sound of tiny water drops, and hit a big bass drum to sound like loud, distant thunder rolling in.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are choreographing a dance about a tiny seed turning into a flower. Describe your first two movements on the stage. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, I would curl up tightly on the floor in a small ball, hugging my knees to pretend I am a tiny seed buried in the dark soil. Then, I would slowly stretch one arm upwards, pretending to be a small green shoot growing toward the bright sunlight.

questions.question_text: How would you tell the story of a brave soldier crossing a snowy mountain using only dance movements and facial expressions? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would walk with slow, heavy, and determined steps to show that climbing the mountain is very hard. My face would look serious, focused, and brave with a tight jaw. I would make lifting motions with my arms to show I am pulling myself up over big, heavy rocks despite the freezing, strong wind pushing against me.

questions.question_text: If you had to create a musical instrument from recycled materials to play at a loud school festival, what would it look like and how would you play it? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would make a giant rattle using a long cardboard tube decorated with bright paint and colorful ribbons. Inside the tube, I would put dried beans, pebbles, and small bells. When I shake it fast, it would make a loud, joyful, and festive rattling sound. Banging it gently on the floor would add a deep, booming beat.
